draft.title: Narrators and reliability
card: First person
a narrator inside the story who says "I" and is a character in it. The reader sees events through that one person's eyes.
Third person

a narrator outside the story who uses "he", "she" or "they". This narrator can be all-knowing, which means they know every character's thoughts. Or they can be limited, which means they follow only one character's thoughts.
Unreliable narrator
a narrator whose account the reader learns not to trust. Clues include contradictions, gaps, strong bias or a view that clashes with what other characters show.
An unreliable narrator invites closer reading. The reader has to work out what is really happening and why the narrator tells it this way.
draft.remember: Ask who is telling the story, how much they know, and whether the reader can trust them.

a.q: In a story, Jai says "I" and tells only what he sees and thinks as he walks home. Which narrator is this?
opts: A first person narrator inside the story
A third person narrator outside the story
An all-knowing narrator outside the story
An unreliable narrator who cannot be trusted
a.why: Jai says "I" and is a character, so the narrator is first person and inside the story. The unreliable option is tempting, but the card says a narrator is unreliable only when clues make the reader doubt the account, and none are given here.
a.clue: Look at the word Jai uses for himself.

b.q: A narrator says she is the most honest person in town. Yet her own story shows her lying to her sister and hiding a letter. What does this most likely invite the reader to do?
opts: Doubt her account and read more closely
Trust her account because she says she is honest
Ignore the narrator and read only the dialogue
Decide the narrator is all-knowing and outside the story
b.why: Her claim clashes with what her own story shows. That contradiction is a clue to an unreliable narrator, so the reader should read more closely. Trusting her because she says she is honest is the tempting mistake, as a narrator's own claims do not make the account reliable.
b.clue: Compare what she says about herself with what she does.

a.best: A first person narrator inside the story

b.best: Doubt her account and read more closely
